chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Dahhak ibn Zayd, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding His Exalted Saying: 'Establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night,' he said: 'Indeed, Allah the Exalted has made obligatory four prayers. Their first time is from the decline of the sun until the middle of the night. Among them are two prayers, their first time is from the decline of the sun until the setting of the sun, except that this one is before that one. And among them are two prayers, their first time is from the setting of the sun until the middle of the night, except that this one is before that one.'

key_terms.لِدُلُوكِ الشَّمْسِ: At the decline of the sun

ai.seo_question: What are the specific start times for the four daily prayers according to this narration?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the Quranic command 'establish prayer from the decline of the sun' by mapping it to the Shia jurisprudential division of the day into four distinct prayer periods. It specifically clarifies that the verse encompasses both the midday prayers (Dhuhr and Asr) and the evening prayers (Maghrib and Isha), establishing the temporal boundaries for each pair within the broader timeframe of sunset to midnight. This interpretation underscores the Shia view that the Quranic verse provides the general framework, while the Imams provide the specific temporal delimitations for the five daily prayers.
